ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a horizontal line segment at y = -2, with the left endpoint approximately at x = -5 and the right endpoint at x = -2, and the endpoints are solid points. There is also a curve branch with an open circle at (-2, 4), passing downward through the region in the figure, with an open circle at (1, -4), then continuing to rise to near x = 3 and connecting with the line segment on the right. The line segment on the right extends from (3, 0) to (5, 2), and at (5, 2) there is a solid point; at x = 3 there is no visible hole or jump. Reasoning: At x = -2, the function value on the graph is given by the solid point as -2, but the value approached from the curve on the right is 4, so x = -2 is already a discontinuity point. The problem states that f is discontinuous at only one x value within the open interval (-5, 5). The curve has an open circle at (1, -4), indicating that when x approaches 1, the function value tends to -4; if f(1) is not -4, then another discontinuity point would be produced at x = 1. Since the only discontinuity point is already x = -2, x = 1 must be continuous, so f(1) must equal that limiting value -4.

Also note the curve and the line segment meet at x = 3 without a visible hole or jump. From the text, f is discontinuous for only one x-value in (-5, 5). Since x = -2 already accounts for that one discontinuity, x = 1 must not be another discontinuity. Therefore the removable hole at (1, -4) must be filled by defining f(1) = -4.
